handoff.purpose: Validate work queue task priority, handle policy-blocked paths, build evidence for candidates, and define auxiliary functions load_inventory, _read_text, _head_sha.

symbols.name: load_inventory
symbols.note: Reads FEATURE_INVENTORY.json, returns dict or empty dict on failure.

symbols.name: _read_text
symbols.note: Reads a text file, returns content or None on OSError.

symbols.name: _head_sha
symbols.note: Reads HEAD SHA from disk git files, returns string or None.

claims.text: Missing, unreadable, not JSON, or JSON that is not an object all degrade to an empty inventory.
claims.why: Code catches OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError and returns {}; also returns {} if data is not dict.

claims.text: The picker's job is to rank work, not to be the thing that breaks when a docs file is mid-edit
claims.why: No code in this chunk relates to ranking work; this is a design statement.

claims.text: an empty queue is a truthful answer to "what does this file tell us", where a traceback is not.
claims.why: No queue logic in this chunk; this is a design rationale.

claims.text: Current HEAD as a full sha, read STRAIGHT OFF DISK, or ``None``.
claims.why: Function signature and initial code show it returns str | None, and reads .git directly.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT ``git rev-parse``. This module spawns no child process at all
claims.why: No import or process spawn visible in this chunk; claim about whole module is uncheckable here.

claims.text: ``test_there_is_no_apply_path_in_this_module`` enforces that by asserting the process-spawning stdlib module is never so much as NAMED in this file
claims.why: No test code or module name check present in this chunk.

claims.text: Handles the three shapes that occur here: ``.git`` as a directory (primary checkout), ``.git`` as a ``gitdir:`` pointer file (linked worktree, where refs live in the shared common dir), and a detached HEAD holding a raw sha.
claims.why: Code checks if dot_git.is_dir() and else branch would handle pointer file and detached HEAD (though full logic not shown, the claim is partially verifiable).

claims.text: Anything unrecognised returns ``None``, which callers read as "cannot tell" and fail OPEN on -- never as "stale".
claims.why: Return None is visible from signature, but callers' behavior is not in this chunk.

observations.what: Priority validation uses float(priority) multiple times; could be simplified.
Import of path_write_blocked is inside the loop, causing repeated imports.
load_inventory uses Path(repo_root) if repo_root else ROOT; ROOT is not defined in this chunk.
_head_sha docstring mentions 'fail OPEN' but no such term is defined in this chunk.
